usage: codecctl [-d | -x] [-p] [-u] [-H val] [-c width] [-f file] [codec|index|default] [sequence...]
	-d	Use decimal register numbers
	-x	Use hex register numbers
	-H	Force headphone detect: true/false
	-p	Ping codec (set exit status based on success)
	-u	Match codec on HAL UID rather than name
	-c	Set the column width (default is to expand to fit screen
	-f	Dump output to file
	-a	Dump all codec settings then quit

Sequence options:	<reg> <value> <sleep_ms> 	Write register
	dump                     	Read all registers
	read <reg>               	Read single register
	read <reg>,<count>       	Read register range
	write <reg> <value>      	Write single register
	mask <reg> <mask> <value>	Mask and write single register
	patch <reg> <mask> <value>	This command can patch a register bitmask value similar to above
	                          	'mask' command format, but only by patching that bitmask value in driver.
	                          	When the underlying driver write a bitmask value during the runtime,
	                          	the (address matched) bitmask patch will be applied. This can be used
	                          	as driver tunable for some parameters, control logic register should
	                          	not be patched.
	patch reset			Remove all register bitmask patch, it will rest the underlying driver to its default behavior.
	patch list			List all patched register bitmask list, it also show how many times underlying
	          			driver actually write the patched bitmask.

Specify no sequence for interactive mode
